reference_sql:
WITH gaps AS (
  -- one row per app event
  SELECT user_id, event_ts, event_name,
    LAG(event_ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_ts, event_id) AS prev_ts
  FROM app_events
)
SELECT event_name AS landing_event, COUNT(*) AS sessions
FROM gaps
WHERE prev_ts IS NULL OR event_ts - prev_ts > INTERVAL '30 minutes'
GROUP BY event_name
alternatives:
WITH gaps AS (
  -- one row per app event
  SELECT user_id, event_ts, event_name,
    LAG(event_ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_ts, event_id) AS prev_ts
  FROM app_events
), flagged AS (
  -- one row per app event
  SELECT user_id, event_ts, event_name,
    CASE WHEN prev_ts IS NULL OR event_ts - prev_ts > INTERVAL '30 minutes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_session
  FROM gaps
)
SELECT event_name AS landing_event, SUM(new_session) AS sessions
FROM flagged
GROUP BY event_name
HAVING SUM(new_session) > 0

SELECT e.event_name AS landing_event, COUNT(*) AS sessions
FROM app_events e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM app_events p
  WHERE p.user_id = e.user_id
    AND (p.event_ts < e.event_ts OR (p.event_ts = e.event_ts AND p.event_id < e.event_id))
    AND p.event_ts >= e.event_ts - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
)
GROUP BY e.event_name

other_way.sql:
SELECT e.event_name AS landing_event, COUNT(*) AS sessions
FROM app_events e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM app_events p
  WHERE p.user_id = e.user_id
    AND (p.event_ts < e.event_ts OR (p.event_ts = e.event_ts AND p.event_id < e.event_id))
    AND p.event_ts >= e.event_ts - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
)
GROUP BY e.event_name
other_way.tradeoff: NOT EXISTS keeps the events with no earlier event of the user in the 30 minutes before, which reads well but runs slower than LAG.
